title: SAML session handshake, token rotation, and admin-driven expiry controls
creator: Ava Morales
description: Define and implement an improved SAML session handshake and token rotation model that aligns SAML assertion lifetimes with Redwood session tokens, supports admin-driven expiry and immediate revocation workflows, and produces enriched audit logs for forensics. This ticket consolidates decisions for JIT provisioning interactions, MFA expectations, logout propagation, and re-auth triggers for high-risk actions.
acceptance_criteria: SAML->Redwood session mapping documented: how assertion conditions (NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter) map to session TTL and refresh windows
Server-side token rotation implemented: short-lived session JWTs rotated with a refresh token flow that is tolerant to network retries and preserves KV cache behavior
Admin console exposes a per-organization session expiry override that immediately marks existing sessions for revocation
Logout propagation supports immediate front-channel and back-channel flows where available; failing that, sessions are marked as forced-reauth and audit logs contain IDP session metadata
Audit events include SAML-idp-id, authn_instant, assertion_id, provisioning outcome, MFA_hint, and revocation_reason
Re-auth policy hooks trigger on role elevation, scoped admin actions, and when the IDP signals step-up (authncontext comparison)
tech_notes: Design decision: use short-lived access JWT (5-15m) + long-lived refresh token (1-14 days) stored server-side; rotation performed on each refresh to prevent reuse.
Map SAML assertion NotOnOrAfter to maximum session age but allow org-level override to shorten TTL; do NOT extend session beyond IDP-provided expiry unless explicit admin policy permits.
JIT provisioning: create user record on first successful assertion but mark 'provisioned_via' and persist assertion_id for audit linkage.
MFA: if IDP asserts MFA in AuthnContextClassRef, treat as primary MFA; otherwise enforce re-auth with Redwood MFA for sensitive flows per policy table (see rollout_plan).
Logout handling: implement best-effort back-channel logout when IDP sends LogoutRequest. For SP-initiated logout, send LogoutRequest and mark session revoked immediately even if handshake fails.
Token rotation edge case: handle clock skew by allowing a 2-minute grace on NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter, record clock-skew events in logs for diagnostics.

Audit log schema: use structured log entries (JSON lines) containing fixed keys: event_type, user_id, idp_entity_id, assertion_id, authn_instant, mfa_hint, session_id, previous_session_state, revocation_cause, request_id
KV cache impact: session rotation must preserve model-serving KV caches keyed by user-session identifier; rotation should update session mapping atomically to avoid cache misses during token swap.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Implement session mapping and audit enrichment behind feature flag for 10% of orgs; monitor reauth/errors for 7 days
Phase 2 (Org opt-in): Add admin console controls (session expiry override, force revoke) and enable for orgs that opt-in via toggle
Phase 3 (Default): Flip feature on for all hosted orgs with migration window of 30 days; provide SDK changes and migration guide
Fallback: If revocation throughput causes datastore pressure, throttle admin-driven mass-revoke and queue background invalidation with status shown in console
risks: Mass revocation can overload session store and auth-service; need rate-limits and background workers
Mismatch between IDP assertion TTL and Redwood refresh token could allow unexpected session durations if not enforced consistently
Failure to capture assertion metadata will reduce forensic value of logs; integration tests must validate end-to-end fields
SP/IDP logout variability across providers (Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin) requires provider-specific heuristics; risk of stale sessions if heuristics are incomplete
testing_plan: Unit tests for mapping rules (NotOnOrAfter -> max_session_age and rotation windows)
Integration tests with mocked IDPs: successful assertion, expired assertion, clock skew, LogoutRequest handling
Chaos test: force network partition during token refresh to ensure atomic swap and cache preservation
Load test: admin mass-revoke 100k sessions across 5 orgs to measure datastore and worker throughput
E2E security test: verify reauth is required for privileged APIs even if session token is valid when 'require_stepup' flag set
